texts: bad: "alongside mire-essence" is recorded as a second thing burned, which the preposition does not license; done correctly it becomes a bare "alongside" side-relation and the sentence then no longer says the mire-essence is burned at all, so that content is lost either way. Rewrite as: "The Stilllight Lantern burns wintergloss and mire-essence for one week." — plain coordination gives each substance its own burning, both for the same week.

bad: "what happens to" leaves the nightmoths in a "to" relation that no statement ever writes, so the question matches nothing about them (the "at the Stilllight Lantern" part is fine). Rewrite as: "What do the nightmoths do at the Stilllight Lantern?" — an open verb with the moths as the doer is the shape the translator handles; if your answer instead has the moths acted on, name the verb, e.g. "Does the Stilllight Lantern burn the nightmoths?".
